summary: Contract change/termination first slice. contracts gains append-only ContractChange (canonical fields: change_type add_scope/reduce_scope/price_change/extension/termination, five statuses, signed deltas, evidence, draft_content, decider/time/note) and ContractChangeReceipt idempotency receipts, plus Contract.terminated_on and contracts migration 0003 with SQLite/PostgreSQL triggers (no deletes; draft revision version+1; a single decision with creator != decider enforced by service and trigger; terminated contracts immutable). save_contract_change_draft and decide_contract_change carry the canonical contracts.contract_change.draft.save/v1 and contracts.change.decide/v1 semantics in a named service/browser workflow: company lock, one approved version required, PH-214 schema validation reuse, server-derived signed deltas checked against client input, termination without replacement content, one draft per contract, replay/changed-input conflict and optimistic version; approval creates a new approved ContractVersion and supersedes the previous one (or terminates the contract without a new version) and emits exactly one contracts.version_approved.v1 (source=new version, changed_refs=[version, change]) and one contracts.change_effective.v1 (source=change; changed_refs=[change, version] or [change, contract] for termination) with posting_event_refs=[]; no new canonical topic/command, no ledger/cash/revenue/open-item write. approved_line_snapshot allows business dates before termination; approved_terms_snapshot rejects settlement on/after terminated_on while posted settlements/open items stay unchanged. Views/forms/templates add change history, draft form, independent decision and contract-detail change area. verify_integrity adds contract-change invariants (status/type/org, approved change exactly one change_effective envelope and matching version/termination state, draft/unapproved cannot carry the effective event, one draft per contract, active contracts exactly one approved version, terminated contracts keep their approved version and date, approved versions have an approval chain and exactly one version_approved envelope). Independent review round 1 rejected three blockers; they are fixed in this branch: (1) creator != decider is now enforced by both vendor triggers and by verify_integrity with forged self-approval regressions; (2) draft edits are allowed for draft_content/evidence/deltas while identity/create fields stay immutable and decision freezes those facts, with an edit regression; (3) ContractChange INSERT triggers reject non-active contracts, verify_integrity rejects terminated-contract/new-change states and validates version_approved changed_refs=[version, change] with forged-event regressions. Independent fresh-context S review round 2 returned PASS with 0 blockers at HEAD 24918f9: creator independence now enforced by both vendor triggers and verify_integrity (forged regression), draft edits work with identity/create fields immutable and decision-time freeze (edit regression approves edited content), and terminated-contract/insert/envelope checks are complete (forged regressions).

findings: ROUND-2 BLOCKERS RESOLVED AND VERIFIED AT 24918f9: (1) creator independence is now enforced in depth: both PostgreSQL and SQLite ContractChange update guards reject `NEW.decided_by_member_id = NEW.created_by_member_id`, verify_integrity adds a `self_decided` assertion for approved/rejected/withdrawn, and forged direct-DB self-approval/self-decided verification regressions pass; the report no longer claims trigger enforcement it does not have. (2) Draft editing now works as advertised: both triggers allow draft->draft changes to draft_content/evidence/net|tax|gross delta with version+1 while identity/contract/change_type/requested_on/created_by/created_at/create_token/create_digest stay immutable, and the decision branch freezes those facts by comparing them to the last draft values; the new regression edits a draft (12000 -> version 2, updated deltas), approves it, and confirms the resulting approved ContractVersion uses the edited 120000 net. (3) termination/event enforcement is complete: both Insert triggers require the referenced contract to be active; verify_integrity rejects drafts/new changes on terminated contracts (local-date comparison), rejects non-termination approved changes after termination, requires exactly one approved termination change, and validates version_approved changed_refs=[version, change] via the approval audit's change_id; forged terminated-draft/self-decided/version_approved-changed_refs regressions pass. The service also now permits rejecting/withdrawing an existing draft after termination while approving still requires an active contract, matching the frozen spec's exception.

CORE BEHAVIOR STILL VERIFIED: ContractChange/ContractChangeReceipt and Contract.terminated_on are append-only/constrained (no delete, single draft, status/type/amount constraints); save_contract_change_draft derives signed deltas from normalized lines and rejects client mismatch, termination-with-content, future dates, duplicate draft, changed-input token replay, expected_version mismatch and non-active contracts; decide_contract_change is company-locked, independent (creator excluded), requires note for reject, terminal rejected/withdrawn without canonical events, and creates a new approved ContractVersion, supersedes the previous approved version, emits exactly one contracts.version_approved.v1 with source=version and changed_refs=[version, change] and exactly one contracts.change_effective.v1 with source=change and changed_refs=[change, version] (or [change, contract] for termination), posting_event_refs=[]; termination keeps the historical approved version, sets terminated_on/status, and approved_terms_snapshot rejects settlement reads on/after terminated_on while allowing earlier as_of and leaving already posted facts untouched; no new canonical topic/command and no ledger/cash/revenue/open-item writes.
